title: AWS session token alone: confidentiality not stated
summary: An AWS session token (long base64-like string) appearing alone in an AWS_SESSION_TOKEN assignment, with no key ID or secret in the input. Value is synthetic.
rationale: The provider documents the session token as the value users must pass to use temporary credentials, but the pages read do not say whether a token separated from its key pair is confidential or what its length and alphabet are. Left open.

expectation.rationale: Unresolved: the STS Credentials type says 'The token that users must pass to the service API to use the temporary credentials' and gives no confidentiality statement, length or alphabet. Would resolve: a provider statement on the session token, or a project-policy decision with a second reviewer. A session-token family is not proposed here; see the PR notes.

sources.supports: SessionToken: the token users must pass to use the temporary credentials; no confidentiality statement

notes: Project-authored by the Redact Secret project, which maintains this repository; not independent evidence. Draft; not yet reviewed.
